chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Earl Dancer, singer and manager who made Ethel Waters
summary: Dancer never led a band; he was an entertainer who took up Ethel Waters and later managed cabarets in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Was that at the same time he led a band?
Earl Dancer led a band, right? He sang and led a band?

No, he didn't lead a band. He become the manager there but he used to be a singer and dancer, you know. He was...he made Ethel Waters. See, he took up with Ethel Waters when she was just singin' around, and he put her in two or three Broadway shows, then they split up, you know.
Yeah, I met Earl Dancer...in the '50s, I think. He was a good friend of Duke Ellington's. I met him with Duke Ellington.
Yeah, he was a good friend of ever'body. He's one of them guys that, "lot of mouth," you know. Yeah. Earl--I knew Earl since we were back in '15, '16, '17. He died up in Elsinores [California].
I knew he died. I didn't know where.
Yeah. That's where he lived all his last few years.
He had a band here in Los Angeles at one time?
Huh! No, he never did have a band.
Yeah, he was a entertainer. That's all.
And, at one point, he operated the Alabam? Or the...
Yeah, you know, he leaded it and ran it. He put a show and things in there, you know.
